title: Method for a new risk assessment of urban inundation: G-DEMATEL–AHP
author: Zheng

steps.title: Construct Direct Influential Relation Matrix
steps.instruction: Create the direct influential relation matrix C'k for the kth expert based on data from the expert questionnaire survey using Eq. (1)–(2) and Eq. (3).

steps.title: Normalize Direct Influential Relation Matrix
steps.instruction: Normalize the kth direct influential relation matrix to obtain Ck using Eq. (4), where Ck = (1 / max(xij,k)) * C'k.

steps.title: Fuzzify Matrix using Grey Theory
steps.instruction: Transform the elements of matrix Ck into grey interval numbers [Ckdown, Ckup] according to Grey theory, following the relationship in Table 4 and Eq. (3)–(5) of the companion study [1] and Eq. (5).

steps.title: Calculate Comprehensive Influential Relation Matrix
steps.instruction: Average the influence scores from all K experts to create the comprehensive influential relation matrix N, consisting of the upper limit matrix (Nup) and lower limit matrix (Ndown) as per Eq. (6) and Eq. (7).

steps.title: Whitenize Grey Interval Numbers
steps.instruction: Convert the comprehensive influential relation matrix [Ndown, Nup] into crisp values (sij) using the whitenization process.

substeps.instruction: Calculate normalized upper and lower bounds using Eq. (8)–(11) or the simplified Eq. (12)–(14) where the minimum value of the upper influential relation matrix is zero.
Calculate the final crisp values (sij) using Eq. (15).

steps.title: Determine Degree of Influence via DEMATEL
steps.instruction: Use the crisp values (sij) to determine the influential and influenced degrees of the factors.

substeps.instruction: Compose the crisp influential matrix (S) as per Eq. (16).
Calculate the total relation matrix (T) using Eq. (17) and the normalized matrix Snor defined in Eq. (18).
Obtain the influential degree (Di) and influenced degree (Ri) for the ith factor using Eq. (19).

steps.title: Calculate Final Weights using AHP
steps.instruction: Establish the AHP comparison matrix (A) through pairwise comparison of Di and follow the AHP calculation procedure (detailed in companion article [1]) to obtain the final weight (wi) for each factor.

steps.title: Validate Risk Assessment Results
steps.instruction: Map the calculated weights using GIS software with actual data to obtain risk level distributions.

substeps.instruction: Compare the distribution with known waterlogging sites (e.g., Zhengzhou flooding disaster on 20 July 2021).
Verify the consistency ratio (CR) of the Ni comparison matrix is less than 0.1.
Compute weights (wi) using MATLAB software based on Eq. (7)–(9) of the companion article [1].
